title: A Decade of Financial Signals, Cash Conversion, and Per-Share Limits

epigraph.quote: Our enterprise analytics software business did not generate positive cash flow from operations.
epigraph.author: Strategy FY2025 Form 10-K

web_blocks.html: A decade of statements is most useful when you begin with cash earned from operations, then separate the balance-sheet expansion and financing activity from customer economics. [1][11]

The table transcribes the annual series in the sanitized SEC company-facts extract for FY2016–FY2025. Monetary values are USD millions. Parentheses are represented as negative values; a dash means the extract has no reported long-term-debt value for that year. These are selected standardized facts, not a substitute for full audited statements or a complete balance-sheet reconciliation. [1][11]

web_blocks.note: All values are USD millions from the permitted sanitized SEC company-facts extract; long-term debt is null for 2016–2020 in that extract. [1][11]

web_blocks.html: The table shows a large balance-sheet shift beside a comparatively flat software revenue base. These company-wide facts do not isolate the software segment or reconcile every balance-sheet classification. Read cash flow and debt alongside the discussion below; total assets are not the same as cash available for operations. [1][11]

web_blocks.title: A stable software revenue scale meets a transformed balance sheet

web_blocks.html: Revenue stayed within a relatively narrow band from 2016 through 2023, moving between $480.735 million and $513.589 million in the supplied series. It fell to $463.456 million in 2024 and was $477.233 million in 2025. The decade therefore does not show a software revenue base that has grown in proportion to the enormous changes in total assets and reported earnings; it shows an established revenue operation alongside a later balance-sheet transformation. The annual facts alone do not assign that expansion to individual asset classes, but the Q3 2026 filing directly reports $70.824 billion of digital assets at September 30. [1][11][2]

Operating income and net income become difficult to read as software-performance series after large digital-asset remeasurements enter the income statement. Operating income was positive in 2016–2018, near break-even or modestly negative in 2019–2020, and substantially negative in 2021, 2022, 2024, and 2025. Net income does not move in lockstep: 2023 shows operating loss of $115.047 million alongside net income of $429.121 million in the facts extract. The permitted extract does not provide the full reconciliation needed to explain that difference, so no single tax, financing, or accounting cause should be invented. [1][11]

web_blocks.title: Cash conversion is uneven, not a synonym for reported earnings

web_blocks.html: Operating cash flow was positive in every year from 2016 through 2021, though it contracted to $3.211 million in 2022, then was $12.712 million in 2023, negative $53.032 million in 2024, and negative $67.241 million in 2025. Against FY2025 capital expenditure of $8.212 million, a simple CFO-less-capex proxy is negative $75.453 million. Capex was lower in earlier years—$2.337 million to $6.846 million in 2016–2018 and $2.486 million in 2022—but that does not make the operating cash pattern smooth. The 10-K specifically says the software business did not generate positive operating cash in FY2025 and was not expected to produce enough to satisfy near-term financial obligations or liquidity needs. [1][11]

The nine-month 2026 comparison is more favorable but still interim. Operating cash flow was positive $14.267 million with capex of $3.181 million, versus negative $45.612 million and capex of $7.628 million in nine-month 2025. Company-wide investing cash flow was negative $17.228 billion and financing cash flow positive $17.418 billion in nine-month 2026; in FY2025 the corresponding annual facts were negative $22.512 billion and positive $24.844 billion. Those large financing and investing movements emphasize that the company’s cash ledger includes treasury activity far beyond the software operation. The summarized facts do not give the transaction-by-transaction bridge, so do not attribute the whole investing outflow to one specific purchase category without the full statement. [1][11][2]

web_blocks.title: Working capital: what a cash-flow diagnosis needs

web_blocks.html: Operating cash flow generally reconciles net income for noncash items and changes in operating assets and liabilities. For a subscription software company, you would examine receivables and collection timing, contract assets, deferred revenue, accrued compensation, payables, taxes, and other working-capital movements, then compare cash collections with recognized revenue. The permitted annual extract provides aggregate operating cash flow but not that detailed bridge; the excerpts likewise do not supply receivables, deferred-revenue, or payables histories. You therefore cannot calculate a ten-year days-sales-outstanding series, identify whether FY2024–FY2025 cash use came mainly from collection timing or expense settlement, or infer the renewal quality of deferred balances. [1][11][2]

There is an additional scope caution. The annual series is a company-level facts extract, while the 10-K statement about FY2025 cash generation specifically addresses the enterprise analytics software business. Consolidated cash can be influenced by treasury purchases, financing proceeds, interest, taxes, and other company activities. The company’s nine-month 2026 CFO improvement is relevant, but the facts packet does not isolate the cash contribution of the software segment. The cleanest conclusion is that consolidated cash conversion was inconsistent and that management separately warned about software cash sufficiency. More detailed segment cash flow and working-capital disclosure would be needed to assign causes. [1][11][2]

The annual operating and net results cannot be interpreted without recognizing the role of digital-asset fair value. The Q3 2026 filing reports a $20.912 billion fair-value gain for the quarter and a $1.858 billion loss for the first nine months, while the company release reports Q3 net income of $19.533 billion and explains that it was substantially due to the digital-asset mark-to-market. The quarter’s result can therefore reverse direction sharply without a comparable change in software customer revenue. Fair-value changes affect accounting income, but are not themselves customer cash receipts; the 10-Q also states that Bitcoin generates no cash flow and incurs custody costs. [2][3]

Balance-sheet totals require equal care. The annual facts show assets increasing from $25.844 billion in 2024 to $61.641 billion in 2025, while cash increased from $38.117 million to $2.301 billion and long-term debt from $7.192 billion to $8.190 billion. By September 30, 2026, the 10-Q reports $2.501 billion cash, $3.404 billion short-term investments, and $70.824 billion digital assets. These are selected reported balances from different dates and should not be added or compared as if all were liquid, risk-free operating resources. The filing explicitly identifies the concentration, custody, and legal and technical uncertainties of the digital assets. [1][11][2]

The selected company-facts extract’s assets, liabilities, and equity columns do not by themselves provide a complete balance-sheet reconciliation. Their definitions may not capture every separate balance-sheet classification needed to reconcile the accounting equation, so you should not use the columns to infer a missing asset or liability. Consult the full audited statements for that work; those were not among the permitted files for this pass. Likewise, a carrying amount is not a cash-flow measure, and a large asset balance is not equivalent to the cash available to pay obligations on a specific date. [1][11][2]

web_blocks.title: Dilution and per-share accounting: a major evidence boundary

web_blocks.html: Management’s seven-year goal is expressed as doubling Bitcoin per share through digital credit. That wording makes per-share measurement essential: an increase in total Bitcoin does not automatically produce the same increase per share if the share count or other claims on the asset change. The permitted fundamentals extract contains no annual basic or diluted share counts, issuance detail, stock-based compensation series, convertible-security conversion terms, or fully diluted share bridge. The Q3 company materials give the goal and aggregate Bitcoin holdings but not enough share data to calculate progress per share or quantify dilution. This chapter therefore identifies the mechanism that must be measured without estimating it. [3][4]

A complete dilution analysis would distinguish issued common shares, potential conversion of debt or preferred instruments, employee awards, repurchases if any, and the timing and consideration for each issuance. It would then compare those claims with the numerator management selected—Bitcoin per share—and with cash obligations such as interest and preferred dividends. The release reports $1.48 billion of cumulative preferred dividends paid and company-described coverage based on USD assets, but does not provide the full share-count or instrument schedule in the supplied excerpt. No per-share conclusion can responsibly be drawn from total Bitcoin accumulation alone. [3][4]

Your ten-year read should remain two-sided. The analytics operation retained a substantial revenue base, with 2025 revenue near the levels in the earlier annual series, and cloud subscriptions grew in the reported comparisons. Yet cash generation weakened in the latest full years, FY2025 software operating cash flow was explicitly insufficient for management’s stated needs, and annual earnings were made volatile by large asset remeasurements. The balance sheet expanded dramatically alongside treasury activity, but aggregate assets do not substitute for operating cash. The next evidence that would most improve the analysis is a segment-level cash bridge, working-capital detail, customer retention and concentration, and full diluted per-share data. [1][11][2][3]

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: The ten-year table contains two stories moving on different clocks: a software revenue base that stayed near half a billion dollars and a balance sheet reshaped by Bitcoin accumulation and financing. Cash conversion and per-share accounting are where you test whether those stories can coexist without letting one conceal the other. [1][11][2][3][4]

book_paragraphs: A ten-year table is not a verdict; it is a map of what changed and what did not. In the sanitized company-facts series, revenue ranges from $463.456 million in 2024 to $513.589 million in 2016 across FY2016–FY2025. The 2025 figure is $477.233 million. Those data describe a software revenue base that remained substantial but did not grow in proportion to the later expansion in reported total assets. The extract does not allocate each year’s revenue to the four streams, so you cannot use it to reconstruct a decade-long cloud transition. [1][11]

The balance sheet changed on a very different scale. Reported assets were $25.844 billion in 2024 and $61.641 billion in 2025; cash in those annual rows was $38.117 million and $2.301 billion respectively, while long-term debt was $7.192 billion and $8.190 billion. The Q3 2026 filing later reports $2.501 billion of cash, $3.404 billion of short-term investments, and $70.824 billion of digital assets as of September 30. These numbers should be read as dated balances, not added indiscriminately or treated as equivalent forms of liquidity. The filing says the vast majority of company assets are concentrated in Bitcoin, which generates no cash flow and carries custody and other risks. [1][11][2]

Operating income and net income also tell different stories across the decade. Operating income was positive in 2016, 2017, and 2018, near zero or modestly negative in 2019 and 2020, and negative thereafter in the reported series. Net income was positive in 2023 even though the same extract shows an operating loss of $115.047 million. Without the full statement reconciliation, you should not assign that divergence to a particular tax benefit, financing item, or accounting event. The prudent observation is that neither net income nor operating income is a clean standalone proxy for software cash economics when the company has large digital-asset remeasurement effects. [1][11]

Cash conversion is more revealing and less smooth. Operating cash flow was positive from 2016 through 2021, fell to $3.211 million in 2022, was $12.712 million in 2023, then turned negative by $53.032 million in 2024 and $67.241 million in 2025. Capital expenditure was relatively small beside revenue, at $8.212 million in 2025, giving a simple operating-cash-flow-less-capex proxy of negative $75.453 million. The 10-K’s statement about the software operation is even more pointed: it did not generate positive operating cash flow in FY2025 and management did not expect enough cash from that business to satisfy financial obligations or liquidity needs over the next twelve months. [1][11]

The latest interim observation is encouraging but should not be promoted to a full-year conclusion. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was positive $14.267 million and capex was $3.181 million, compared with negative $45.612 million of CFO and $7.628 million of capex for nine-month 2025. That is a marked improvement over the same duration. The supplied figures do not show whether the improvement was driven by customer collections, timing of payments, noncash adjustments, or other components, nor whether it persisted through year-end. Keep a like-for-like interim comparison and an audited annual history in separate columns. [2]

Working-capital analysis is where the limits of the extract become decisive. Operating cash flow typically reflects net income adjusted for noncash charges and changes in operating assets and liabilities. A software analyst would inspect receivables, contract assets, deferred revenue, payables, accrued compensation, taxes, and the timing of collections against recognized revenue. The permitted source does not supply those lines across the decade, and the cited filing excerpts do not provide a full working-capital bridge. You cannot responsibly calculate ten years of days sales outstanding, decide that customers are paying more slowly, or attribute the cash deficit to deferred revenue reversals. The required account-level evidence is absent. [1][11][2]

Another limitation is the boundary between segment and consolidated cash. The 10-K statement about FY2025 speaks specifically to the enterprise analytics software operation’s cash generation. The annual facts series reports company-wide operating cash flow. Meanwhile, annual cash from investing was negative $22.512 billion and cash from financing positive $24.844 billion in 2025; for the first nine months of 2026 the corresponding totals were negative $17.228 billion and positive $17.418 billion. These large flows reflect a company with substantial treasury and financing activity, but the permitted summary does not list each transaction. Do not equate consolidated CFO with segment cash, and do not allocate all investing outflow to a single purpose without the full cash-flow statement. [1][11][2]

Accounting volatility is visible in the recent interim period. Q3 2026 included a $20.912 billion digital-asset fair-value gain, while the first nine months of 2026 showed a $1.858 billion fair-value loss. Q3 net income was $19.533 billion and the company release says it was substantially explained by the digital-asset mark-to-market. The annual facts likewise show large swings in operating and net results alongside a business whose reported software revenue is measured in hundreds of millions. A fair-value gain can raise accounting earnings without being a cash receipt from a software customer; a subsequent loss can reverse reported results without showing an equivalent deterioration in software usage. [2][3]

The asset’s non-cash nature should not be mistaken for irrelevance. It changes reported income, contributes to the balance-sheet composition, and carries its own risks. The 10-Q says Bitcoin produces no cash flow and cites legal, commercial, regulatory, technical, counterparty, custody, and cybersecurity uncertainties. As of September 30, 2026, digital assets had a $70.824 billion carrying amount. You therefore need two views at once: an operating scorecard that isolates software revenue and cash conversion, and a consolidated balance-sheet view that recognizes a concentrated asset with non-operating cash characteristics. Neither can stand in for the other. [2]

The balance-sheet facts extract is not a substitute for a full audited statement. Its selected asset, liability, and equity series do not independently reconcile to one another in each displayed row. The extract does not explain every classification or provide all possible equity-related components. You should flag this as a source limitation rather than inventing a missing liability, assuming the equity tag is comprehensive, or treating the table as a formal accounting-equation proof. Likewise, cash, short-term investments, and digital assets are distinct balances with different liquidity, volatility, and custody attributes. [1][11][2]

Per-share dilution is a particularly important evidence gap because management’s stated treasury objective is per share. On the Q3 call, Le said, “The goal is to double Bitcoin per share in seven years through the use of digital credit.” If total Bitcoin grows while common shares or other claims expand, total holdings and per-share holdings can move at different rates. The permitted annual extract does not contain annual basic or diluted share counts, stock-based compensation, conversion terms, instrument-level issuance, or a fully diluted share bridge. The company release gives aggregate Bitcoin holdings and the objective, but not the data needed to calculate progress toward it. You can identify the required test; you cannot perform it here. [3][4]

A proper per-share bridge would list common shares outstanding over time, potential shares from conversion instruments and awards, preferred claims, debt terms, and relevant cash obligations. It would then compute the specified Bitcoin-per-share measure using a clearly defined numerator and denominator. Management’s use of “digital credit” should not be treated as synonymous with common-share issuance; the available excerpts do not provide enough instrument detail to make that claim. The release does report $1.48 billion in cumulative preferred dividends paid and a company-described 3.4 years of dividend-plus-interest coverage as of October 25, but it does not furnish the full capital-structure schedule required to model future dilution or claims. [3][4]

The annual table also prevents a common analytical shortcut: using net income as cash. For 2023, the extract lists net income of $429.121 million and CFO of $12.712 million; for 2025 it lists net loss of $3.848 billion and CFO of negative $67.241 million. Those gaps demonstrate that earnings and cash can diverge materially, but the extract does not contain enough detail to explain every divergence. A quality review would reconcile noncash fair-value adjustments, taxes, working-capital changes, and financing costs from full statements before describing normalized cash generation. This Pass 1 can flag the need and show the reported figures; it cannot fabricate that reconciliation. [1][11][2]

The clean way to keep those questions organized is to avoid collapsing balance-sheet growth into business quality. For software, ask what share of recognized revenue turns into collected cash after service and operating costs. For treasury activity, ask how assets, custody, financing, and per-share claims interact. For consolidated liquidity, reconcile all cash-flow categories and obligations. A ten-year table gives you the starting pattern, but only fuller account-level disclosures can explain causation. In particular, no days-sales-outstanding series should be reverse-engineered from annual revenue and cash flow when receivables and working-capital balances are absent. [1][11][2][3][4]

Your decade-long conclusion should therefore be careful. Strategy preserved an enterprise software revenue base around the same broad scale through 2025, and its cloud subscription line grew in the supplied FY2024–FY2025 and Q3 comparisons. Cash generation was more uneven, with negative consolidated CFO in both latest annual periods and an explicit warning about software cash needs. Meanwhile, digital-asset remeasurement and financing changed the consolidated balance sheet and earnings profile. The most valuable missing evidence is a full segment cash-flow bridge, detailed working-capital data, customer retention and concentration, and diluted per-share history. Those gaps mark the boundary of this dossier’s permitted fundamentals pass. [1][11][2][3]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A large balance sheet is not automatically an operating cash engine. The decade’s useful question is whether customer activity generates durable cash while treasury assets and financing are measured on their own terms. [1][11][2]

book_callouts.title: EVIDENCE LIMIT
book_callouts.text: No ten-year DSO series, detailed working-capital bridge, or diluted-share history is present in the permitted data. Management’s per-share objective can be named, but progress and dilution cannot be quantified in this pass. [1][11][3][4]
